proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly lists Dameli -sā̃ genitive suffix under santaka belonging to, section 1, alongside Kati genitive -st(e), Sindhi -sando and older Punjabi sandā. Perder treats modern sā̃ as an independent animate possessive marker rather than a suffix and shows feminine sā̃ĩ/-i agreement with the possessed noun. These are ordinary forms of the same grammatical word, not separate derivations. Preserve the source difference in grammatical analysis. The Kati parallel supplies a Nuristani connection, not evidence of a particular borrowing direction.

Perder explicitly places suna/suni in the plural-possessor cells of the same paradigm as sā̃/sā̃ĩ, with final -i agreeing with a feminine possessed noun. This supports extending the santaka-family analysis to the plural allomorphs, but Turner’s Dameli citation is specifically singular -sā̃ and the plural u-vowel is not explained there. This is a less direct paradigm-based proposal, retained separately for review; it is not a derivation from the modern singular. Compare the same Kati -st(e) and Sindhi -sando family without asserting Nuristani borrowing.

approval: User: approve all; prefer Pashto where best matched, then Urdu for broadly Perso-Arabic terms. Approval includes qualified analyses, not a claim that uncertainties are resolved.
donor_policy: Prefer an attested Pashto donor where form and meaning fit best; otherwise prefer Urdu for broadly shared Perso-Arabic loans. Preserve explicit source attribution, phonological uncertainty and possible Nuristani mediation. Do not substitute a different dialect merely because its node is linkable.
